s: As per the Noise standards for fire-crackers notified by the Environment (Protection) (Second Amendment) Rules, 2006), the manufacture, sale or use of fire-crackers generating noise level exceeding ____ at 4 meters distance from the point of bursting shall be prohibited.
x: Crackers louder than 125 dB(AI) or 145 dB(C)pk at 4 m from the point of bursting may not be made, sold or used (EP Rules standard, amended 2006).

s: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of planting trees for poor communities in India?
o: Trees rapidly improve the local climate by providing shade, reducing the temperature, and promoting rainfall.
Trees improve soil quality through composting, water retention, and reduction of soil erosion.
Trees absorb the excess noise from small industries and irrigation facilities.
Trees give rural families a source of sustainable income and nutritious food.
x: Trees give shade and moderate local climate, improve soil and give income and food. Absorbing noise from small industries and irrigation is not counted as a benefit of tree planting for poor communities.

s:
Consider the following statements with reference to GlobLitter Partnerships Project:

I. It is an initiative of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).

II. It aims to reduce marine litter, especially plastic litter from all the sources.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: GloLitter Partnerships is run by the IMO and FAO (funded by Norway), not UNEP. It targets sea-based plastic litter from shipping and fisheries, not litter from all sources. So neither statement is correct.

s: Which radioactive pollutant drew the attention of public, due to its occurrence in the building material?
x:
Most quiz keys: Thorium. Strictly, the building-material concern that drew public attention is radon-222 (indoor gas from uranium/thorium decay in bricks, granite, soil) – PMF Environment Part 4 p.2; Shankar Part 6 radon note.
Building materials such as granite, bricks and fly ash carry thorium (with uranium and K-40); the printed and commonly given answer is thorium. Its decay gas radon is what accumulates indoors.

s:
Which of the following statements about radioactive pollution are correct?

I. It causes hereditary changes in the animal.

II. It causes disbalance among different minerals in the soil.

III. It hinders blood circulation.

IV. It causes carcinogenesis.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
Codes
x:
Official/most-told key: I, III and IV. Rocket Environment p.63, NextGen 11 p.6 and Shankar Part 7 p.5 list only hereditary changes and cancer, which would give I and IV.
Radioactive pollution causes hereditary (genetic) changes and cancer. Heavy radiation also damages blood-forming tissue and blood vessels, which is why the official key counts statement III as well. Mineral imbalance in soil is not an effect.

s:
Which of the following is/are NOT the method(s) to control soil pollution?
i. Waste should be treated before dumping it in special pits
ii. Setting up of watersheds
iii. Use of pesticides should be minimised
iv. Employing crop rotation options:
x: Treating waste before dumping, minimising pesticides and crop rotation all control soil pollution. Setting up watersheds is a soil and water conservation step, not a soil-pollution control, so only ii is the answer.

s: What is the primary application of bioremediation?
x: Bioremediation is used mainly to clean contaminated soil (and groundwater), using microbes or plants to break down oil, pesticides and solvents. It is not a tool for noise, air or waterborne disease.

src: Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fisheries
s: Heavy metal contamination of the soil cannot be removed by?
x: Immobilisation, soil washing and phytoremediation remove or lock up heavy metals. Simply leaving land fallow does not remove them.

s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Dark Reserve is a public or private land with a distinguished nocturnal environment and starry nights that has been developed responsibly to prevent light pollution.

II. World's 1st International Dark Sky Reserve is Mont-Megantic, located in Russia.

III. The International Dark-Sky Association (IDSA) is a US-based non-profit organisation that designates sites as international dark sky places.

IV. The Department of Science & Technology (DST) has announced the setting up of India's 1st Dark-Sky Reserve in Himachal Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement I (definition) and III (the US-based IDA, now DarkSky International, certifies sites) are correct. II is wrong (Mont-Mégantic is in Canada) and IV is wrong (India's first reserve is Hanle, Ladakh). No option offers 'I and III only', so 'None of the above' is the key.
